messages:
samir: Heads-up — noticed a p99 jump in nightly bench after the kernel routing PR landed (PR #4217). baseline p99 ~45ms -> 120ms on tails. Anyone on call?

maya: ugh. saw the alert. can you share the bench id and the payload distribution?

samir: bench id: nightly-attn-2026-03-19. input mix is mixed short/long (tokens 8/128/1024) — tail weight ~12%. Full run attached in bench-bot logs: `https://internal/bench/1968881234`

pranav: quick question — did we change sampling or the harness seeding? small nondet sampling can skew p99.

samir: no seed change. CI shows kernel-routing TTL was enabled: route_by_latency:true fallback=kernel_variant_b. suspect routing oscillation at concurrency spike.

lee: can we get a micro-run reproducer? run with `bench-harness --profile=tail --seed=42 --concurrency=64 --routes=all` and paste logs.

samir: running now — tail pass...

bench-bot: Summary: p50=12ms p90=28ms p95=44ms p99=118ms throughput=850rps

maya: key thing: p99 increased but throughput stayed similar. suggests scheduling/backpressure not pure model slowdown. maybe kernel warmup mismatch or kv-cache eviction.

pranav: hypothesis A: continuous-batching groups seeds with same route; routing split introduces head-of-line blocking when batch contains mixed kernels. Hypothesis B: mismatch in kernel quantization path causing slower aten kernel on long sequences.

lee: to test A: run with `--force-routing=static` (everything to fast-kernel) and compare. to test B: run `--force-quant=fp16` v `int8` on same runs.

samir: quick logs from a spike (excerpt):
```
2026-03-19T03:12:01.234Z [runtime] batch_id=9876 route=dynamic fast_kernel=32 slow_kernel=32 wait_ms=72
2026-03-19T03:12:01.234Z [runtime] kv_cache_miss=true eviction=true
2026-03-19T03:12:01.235Z [kernels] slow_kernel p99=210 ms
```

maya: ok eviction + mixed kernels = nasty. ops-bot, did any autoscaler events coincide?

ops-bot: Autoscaler: scaled_up 2 nodes at 03:11:58 UTC due to queue_length spike. No remainder logs.

pranav: sounds like routing + autoscale race. When new nodes join, routing updates and we might interleave kernel variants in batches. We should ensure batch formation is per-kernel affinity.

samir: agree. immediate mitigation: enable `force-static-route` for nightly for 24h and run the experiment. If p99 falls back -> routing code is culprit.

maya: I'll flip the flag on nightly and kick off two runs: static and dynamic with same seeds. assigning: maya -> run experiments, pranav -> add instrumentation for batch composition (per-batch kernel histogram), lee -> prepare quick patch to make batcher respect kernel_affinity.

pranav: instrument PR in progress: logs per-batch: `batch_size, kernel_map, wait_ms, kv_evictions` and add a p99 per-kernel metric.

lee: patch ready but keep as opt-in: `--kernel-affinity=prefer`. can land behind feature flag.

samir: timeline: do runs in the next 2 hours, meet after to decide rollback or canary. if static reduces p99 by >30% -> rollback routing change from canary.

maya: noted. starting run 1 (static) now. will post links.

samir: thanks. if anyone sees anything else, call it out. :thumbsup:
